layers.basics: AM varies carrier amplitude, FM varies frequency, PM phase. FM resists amplitude noise.
layers.deeper: AM bandwidth 2B; FM Carson’s rule B≈2(Δf+f_m); broadcast radio and TV audio use them.
layers.expert: Modulation index β=Δf/f_m; SNR improvement of FM above threshold ∝3β²; envelope and quadrature detectors; SSB and VSB save bandwidth.

title: Digital modulation: ASK, FSK, PSK, QAM, OFDM

layers.basics: Digital modulation switches amplitude, frequency or phase between a few states; QAM mixes amplitude and phase to send many bits per symbol.
layers.deeper: Constellation diagrams display the states; OFDM splits the data across many narrow subcarriers to resist multipath.
layers.expert: 16-QAM carries 4 bits/symbol; OFDM implemented with IFFT, cyclic prefix; peak-to-average power ratio problem; spectral efficiency vs SNR trade-off.

title: Noise, SNR and bit error rate

layers.basics: Noise blurs received symbols; the bit error rate depends on signal-to-noise ratio and modulation type.
layers.deeper: BPSK BER=Q(√(2E_b/N₀)); higher-order modulations need more SNR.
layers.expert: E_b/N₀ vs SNR relation SNR=(E_b/N₀)(R_b/B); Q-function tail of Gaussian; waterfall curves.

title: Information theory: entropy and channel capacity

layers.basics: Entropy measures information in bits; Shannon showed that every noisy channel has a capacity below which errors can be made arbitrarily small.
layers.deeper: C=B log₂(1+SNR); more bandwidth or more power raises capacity, with diminishing returns.
layers.expert: H=−Σp log p; channel coding theorem; Shannon limit −1.59 dB on E_b/N₀ as bandwidth → ∞; turbo and LDPC codes approach it.

layers.basics: Extra check bits let a receiver detect and fix errors; Hamming codes fix single-bit errors; CRCs detect them.
layers.deeper: Block codes work on fixed chunks; convolutional codes work on streams, decoded with the Viterbi algorithm.
layers.expert: Minimum distance d_min corrects ⌊(d−1)/2⌋ errors; Reed–Solomon (QR codes, CDs); LDPC and polar codes in 5G; coding gain.

layers.basics: FDM gives each user a frequency slot, TDM a time slot, CDMA a code; OFDMA mixes slots in time and frequency.
layers.deeper: Cell phones have used all of these across generations.
layers.expert: Orthogonal codes (Walsh); processing gain=chip rate/bit rate; near–far problem; OFDMA in 4G/5G.

title: Wireless channels, fading and link budgets

layers.basics: Signals weaken with distance, bounce off buildings (multipath) and fade in and out as you move.
layers.deeper: Link budget adds transmit power, antenna gains, losses and noise to find received SNR.
layers.expert: Free-space path loss (4πd/λ)²; Rayleigh/Rician fading; delay spread and coherence bandwidth; Doppler; shadowing; Friis & noise figure.

title: Networking basics: OSI model and TCP/IP

layers.basics: Networks are organised in layers: physical, link, network (IP), transport (TCP/UDP), application. Each layer handles one job.
layers.deeper: Packets carry addresses; routers forward them; TCP gives reliable delivery, UDP quick delivery.
layers.expert: Ethernet/Wi-Fi at layer 2; IPv4/v6; congestion control (AIMD, BBR); NAT; TLS; latency-bandwidth product.
